content.text: {"issues":[{"where":"Research Question 4 / Phase 4","problem":"Trial bottles from Phase 3 are filled at month 6–8, so month-10 validation gives only 2–4 months of post-trial storage, which is too short to confirm delay of the peroxide threshold crossing that historically occurs between months 3–5; secondary markers at month 10 will not yet show whether the intervention works across the full shelf-life.","fix":"Either start trial fills earlier (end of Phase 2) so Phase 4 validation covers at least 5 months of storage, or reframe Question 4 to use Rancimat induction period as a surrogate endpoint rather than requiring real-time threshold crossing."},{"where":"Phase 2 — headspace oxygen measurement","problem":"The plan has the university renting a portable oxygen analyser, but this is new work the plan creates on-site at the company's bottling line; however, the company's contributions in the term sheet list 'access to bottling line for headspace oxygen measurement' without specifying who supplies the measurement instrument, leaving a gap if rental falls through or is out of scope for the contract fee.","fix":"Add a sentence to Phase 2 specifying that the oxygen analyser and its rental cost are the university's responsibility under 'analytical consumables,' or confirm the instrument source explicitly in the plan."},{"where":"Research Question 2","problem":"Asking whether tocopherol levels at bottling predict Rancimat induction period across batches, with only three batches in Phase 1, gives too few data points to support a predictive relationship; a correlation across three lots cannot be distinguished from chance.","fix":"Reframe Question 2 as a descriptive comparison ('Do batches with higher tocopherol content show longer Rancimat induction periods?') or expand sampling to at least five to six batches to support the predictive claim."}],"unconfirmed":[]}
